methodology_baseline: Composite Financial Resilience Framework (DORA, Basel III, NIST CSF 2.0)

justifications.default: Financial sector benchmarks demand high baseline maturity (Level 4 - Managed) driven by stringent regulatory frameworks (EU Digital Operational Resilience Act - DORA, SEC Cyber Disclosure, FFIEC guidelines). Core banking transaction processing, automated multi-region active-active resilience, and continuous threat monitoring are non-negotiable operational requirements.
justifications.T1: High maturity (4.10) mandated by zero-downtime banking facility standards, dual-fed UPS rings, and continuous telemetry.
justifications.T2: Mature private cloud and container orchestration (3.90) supporting low-latency transaction processing and regulatory isolation.
justifications.T3: Secure, deterministic enterprise WAN and trading network fabric (3.85) with strict microsegmentation.
justifications.T4: High-durability storage clusters with synchronous multi-site replication and strict data-at-rest encryption (4.00).
justifications.T5: Demanding operational resilience and automated disaster recovery switchover (4.15) with sub-second RPO objectives.
justifications.T6: Advanced cybersecurity posture (4.25) enforcing continuous behavioral threat analytics, zero-trust identity, and Tier-0 PAM governance.
justifications.T7: Relational transactional databases and core banking ledger integrity (3.95) with automated reconciliation.
justifications.T8: Strict data governance, privacy compliance (GDPR/GLBA), and automated regulatory reporting pipelines (4.05).
justifications.T9: Secure workplace endpoints with zero-trust network access, conditional access policies, and enterprise DLP (3.85).
justifications.T10: Fiduciary IT governance, automated cloud financial controls (FinOps), and rigorous vendor audit mechanisms (3.90).
